_comment: A worked cross-codebase example: the Android half of an Android ↔ iOS pair.
It exists to show the three parity shapes on real-looking nodes. Build it with:
then query it, e.g. CODEBASE_KG_PATH=/tmp/example.db uv run --no-project --quiet mcp/launch/kg_cli.py query kg_parity_gaps
See SCHEMA.md §9 for the parity contract.

nodes.description: Persisted bookmark in the saved_articles table, indexed by articleId for dedup.
nodes._note: MATCHED — SwiftData @Model on the iOS side. Platform tooling differing is expected and is not divergence.

nodes.description: Queries saved_articles: observeAll, findByUrl, insert, deleteByUrl, count.
Bookmarks list; renders saved articles with swipe-to-delete and an empty state.
Backs the bookmarks screen; exposes the saved list as state and removes entries.
Ranks the feed by freshness, breaking flag and normalized source/category weight; stable sort, identity on cold start.
nodes.divergence: Android: pure, persisted signals, wired into the feed. iOS: actor, in-memory, unwired.
nodes._note: DIVERGENT — both sides have it, implemented differently enough to flag. counterpart AND divergence are both required here.

nodes.description: Loads articles, applies the ranker, and exposes feed state with pull-to-refresh.
Time-windowed warm-amber theme applied between local sunset and sunrise.
nodes._note: ANDROID-ONLY — iOS mentions this in a product doc, but there is no code. A doc mention does not count; verify against source. NO counterpart, NO divergence.

nodes.description: Single activity host; sets the theme and hosts the navigation graph.
